input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: With no positional arguments, all() over an empty list returns True, so an empty 'Positional arguments' section heading is now emitted.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with no Argument parameters, which is common. The old code only wrote the section when args was non-empty. The new guard passes vacuously, so formatter.section is entered with no rows and the heading appears in help output for commands that take no positional arguments. Impact: a spurious empty section header in the help text of many commands.
critique: The finding names the same faulty all() guard and one of the label's failure paths: all([]) is vacuously true, so commands with no arguments print an empty 'Positional arguments' header. It does not mention the mixed-help case, but the operation and how it goes wrong are the same.
